visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 final portable frames including the compact 1024×640 preview. Present-day Blue Mosque in Tabriz: broad warm-brick main dome and smaller rear dome, low brick ranges with selected shallow roof cupolas, tall pointed entrance with surviving blue tile bands and broad pale exposed patches, short flat corner tower stumps, pale stone plinth and seven estimated entry steps. The main and dome plans retain current map geometry. Corrected the portal crest triangulation and outward roof normals, added intermediate 2.5 m footing stations to follow terrain dips, moved tile fields ahead of the mapped piers, kept the entry steps clear of an artificial horizontal arch floor, closed the rear screen and placed drum vents on their actual LOD wall faces. Raised the plinth camera above the local ground. Fine mosaic motifs, epigraphy, muqarnas, historical tall minarets, temporary scaffolding/snow, forecourt furniture and furnished interiors are omitted.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all 11 final shared-material/geographic-flat views and north-up placement overlay. Five existing shared 256² brick, raw limestone, mosaic tile, lime plaster and plain wood graphs serve seven merged roles including local opaque blue-grey vents. Dome and wall reuse the brick graph with distinct linear tints; metric UVs provide material scale. Portal remnants use coarse original geometry/tints, not a photograph or copied tile artwork. Every graph is read once and eviction disposes the model geometry/restores host ground. The original anchor and heading remain unchanged. The main footprint and its two dome controls are replaced; twenty separate nearby features, including Azerbaijan Museum and the bazaar, remain host content. Two ground openings cover the mapped structure plus a small estimated threshold inside the entrance recess. Flat placement is a pose/cutout test, not surveyed grade.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 27 final medium-fi views and the matched skyline at full size: Economy/High, noon/late light, three distances, untextured silhouette, six details, four matched LODs and four transitions. Skyline keeps the two brick domes, pointed blue-accent entrance and short corner stumps within the indented main outline. District restores side cupolas and sparse drum vents, street restores more curve/field detail and plinth panels, and closeup refines the portal and dome profiles. Simple brick surfaces spend their detail in shared textures; the budget ceilings are not triangle-fill targets. Coarser dome faceting and loss of small tile patches are intentional distance changes. Synthetic stone neighbors and standard coarse DEM are fixtures; physical phone/tablet/laptop and full-city performance measurements remain pending.
